description.narrative: Stöd inom WASH för utsatta grupper i Kumchon, Nordkorea.

The overall objective of the programme is to improve the health and nutritutional status of vulnerable populations in Kumchon County through increased access to safe drinking water, improved sanitation and improved hygiene practices.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2014Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: Based on the final report it is Sida's assessment that the intervention has reached its outcome objectives. The specific objective of the project was to increase access to safe drinking water and improve sanitation and improve hygiene practices of the target population in Kumchon county town, DPRK. To monitor and establish the results reached a combination of qualitative and quantitative methods have been used. 1) In relation to water quantity and quality: the renovated and constructed water supply systems provide 5061 litres/ day/person, as per tests of water meters and corroborated by household level interviews. According to recent water quality tests from the water source, reservoir intake, distribution reservoirs and random samples from household taps and storage facilities there is zero coliform bacteria and other physical and chemical parameters are within WHO guidelines. 2) In relation to sanitation and hygiene practices: there is less reliance on open defecation or the use traditional shallow pits thanks to the constructed institutional and communal latrines. Hygiene promotion training has been performed. It is too early to assess the longer term outcome in relation to the construction of garbage collection containers but the production of efficient organic manure will undoutedly increase agriculture production as well as reduce health risks. Anecdotal evidence shows that there has been a reduction in Kumchon in the last few years in relation to the incidence of disease, and especielly diarrhoeal. This anecdotal evidence can however not be corroborated by data because of the limited opportunities in the DPRK to access key health related indicators.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
